supported_claims.text: 字 now means a written character or word, but its structure belongs to an older meaning: raising or nurturing a child. 宀 is a roof and 子 is the child beneath it. 子 also supplies sound, so the character combines a meaningful scene with a pronunciation relationship.
The roof and child convey the older meaning together, while 子 also acts as the phonetic component.
Sound comparison for 子: zǐ / zì (Mandarin (pinyin)).

disagreements.text: The path from nurturing to “written character” is not fully settled. A connection through producing or generating is possible, but a different word root has also been proposed. An intermediate story about education should therefore not be treated as a securely demonstrated sequence.
